study.title: Reconsidering the Mechanism of Proton Pump Inhibitor-Associated Fundic Gland Polyps: Absence of Re-enlargement during Potassium-Competitive Acid Blocker Therapy

cover.headline: One type of acid blocker **may shrink polyps where another grew them**, even with higher gastrin levels.

slides.title: If you developed stomach polyps on a PPI, switching drug classes might change their course.
slides.body:
Fundic gland polyps often go together with long-term proton pump inhibitor use. High gastrin from acid suppression has been blamed.

A newer acid blocker raised gastrin even higher. The polyps still shrank, suggesting the link is more than gastrin alone.

slides.title: One woman's fundic gland polyps regressed after switching from rabeprazole to a PCAB, with no re-growth.
slides.body:
The polyps grew over seven years on the PPI rabeprazole. Four months after switching to vonoprazan, they had regressed markedly.

Gastrin stayed elevated during PCAB therapy—491.9 and 753.7 pg/mL—yet the polyps did not return.

slides.title: The timing is unclear, so regression may have started when the PPI was stopped, not when the PCAB began.
slides.body:
The woman briefly used an H2-receptor antagonist between drugs. Regression was first documented four months into PCAB use.

Long-term PCAB therapy was not linked to polyp re-enlargement, despite potent acid suppression and elevated gastrin.

caveats: This is a single case report in one woman, not a controlled study across many people.
This study found a pattern, not a cause. Something else could explain the link.
The exact timing of polyp regression is unknown, so the PCAB may not be solely responsible.

source.abstract: Fundic gland polyps (FGPs) may enlarge during long-term proton pump inhibitor (PPI) therapy, potentially in association with acid suppression and hypergastrinemia. Potassium-competitive acid blockers (PCABs) provide potent and sustained acid suppression and may induce comparable or greater elevations in serum gastrin levels than PPIs. We report a case of FGPs in which regression was documented after changes in acid-suppressive therapy, with no subsequent re-enlargement during long-term use of PCABs. A woman in her 60s with gastroesophageal reflux disease developed progressive enlargement of FGPs during 7 years of rabeprazole therapy. Rabeprazole was discontinued because of marked redness of the enlarged FGPs and concern for possible bleeding and was replaced with an H2-receptor antagonist. After reintroduction of rabeprazole, treatment was switched to a PCAB because of insufficient symptom control. Four months after PCAB initiation, esophagogastroduodenoscopy demonstrated marked regression of the FGPs, with no subsequent re-enlargement during continued PCAB therapy. Serum gastrin levels were elevated at both measurements during PCAB use (491.9 and 753.7 pg/mL). Histological examination revealed similar fundic gland changes characteristic of FGPs in both a residual polyp and the endoscopically non-polypoid background mucosa, without dysplasia. Because the exact timing of FGP regression could not be determined, the regression observed 4 months after vonoprazan initiation cannot be solely attributed to vonoprazan therapy and may have occurred, at least in part, during the preceding period of PPI discontinuation. Nevertheless, no subsequent re-enlargement was observed during long-term vonoprazan therapy. Clinical Trial Registration: Clinical trial registration was not applicable because this was a single case report.
